speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Volunteer Special Constabulary (VSC) is an integral part of the Singapore Police Force (SPF) and has been so for the last 70 years.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In 2008, the VSC strength was slightly over 1,000 officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our VSC officers come from all walks of life: university students, taxi drivers, accountants and lawyers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They have the same powers, they put on the same uniform and perform the same duties, similar to those of regular Police Officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They are deployed for frontline duties at Police Land Divisions, Neighbourhood Police Centres, Traffic Police and also deployed for major events like the National Day Parade.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: VSC officers face personal danger and risks in their line of work similar to regular Police Officers and they undergo rigorous basic training, twice a week in the evenings, over 24 weeks.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: After passing out from training, these officers have to contribute a minimum of 16 hours a month.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On average, each VSC officer contributes about 32 hours a month and they are not paid salaries.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Instead, they are given a small allowance and that is to offset out-of-pocket expenses, such as transport and food.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In 2007, the Police Force conducted a review of this allowance.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At that time, the allowance was $2.80 per hour.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SPF recommended to increase the VSC allowance rate from $2.80 per hour to $3.60 per hour.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The reasons for the increase were considered and evaluated at the Ministry headquarters (HQ) and it were approved by the Permanent Secretary (PS).

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: However, the officers did not take the next step of seeking approval from the Minister, as was required under the Police Force Act.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Within a Ministry, the PS is the Chief Executive Officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He is the Accounting Officer for the Ministry's budget, which runs into several billions of dollars.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, the budget for this year for the Ministry of Home Affairs is $5.34 billion.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The PS also has the authority to approve expenditures up to $10 million.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The decision to increase the VSC allowance in 2008 was taken at the highest senior civil servant level in the Ministry and, in money terms, well within the PS' authority.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But the Police Force Act requires the Minister to approve the increase.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In addition, SPF had also paid allowances for VSC duty beyond the four-hour cap stipulated in the Regulations; and pro-rated allowance for duty for less than an hour.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Since the payments had been made without the Minister's personal approval, AGO classified them as overpayments.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is how AGO has put it, since the Minister's approval should have been obtained.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But it will be fair to describe what happened as a procedural error.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When assessing the nature of the error, the following points need to be considered: (a) the policy intent was to increase the allowance; (b) Ministry HQ agreed that the allowance should be raised and approved this; (c) no one in his right mind could complain or suggest that the VSC officers should not get $3.60 per hour as allowance for their out-of-pocket expenses.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Indeed, most people will consider it as underpayment; (d) nor can anyone reasonably say that it is wrong for the officers to get the allowance, if they volunteered for more than four hours; or that it is wrong if pro-rated payments were made when they volunteered for less than an hour.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: After the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) findings were brought to my attention, I agreed with the rationale for the payments.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It was right that the payments should have been made.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We sought advice from the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC).

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: AGC advised that under the Police Force Act, I can authorise the payment retrospectively, and I authorised the payments.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Regulations were amended, with some provisions deleted, also in accordance with AGC's advice.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I should add that I have asked my staff to review the VSC allowance rate further.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is not a case of officers making decisions to increase allowances and deliberately bypassing the Minister.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The officers responsible for handling the earlier approval have been spoken to about their mistake.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our VSC officers have been doing good work for many years.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They work alongside our regular Police Officers, hand in hand.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SSGT(V) Mohamad Ariff Bin Said Abdul Kader, aged 36, is a Project Manager in the construction industry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Despite his busy schedule juggling a full-time job and looking after his family, he performs frontline policing duties on Fridays and Saturdays in the evenings.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He does so with regular counterparts from the Jurong Police Division.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Another VSC officer is 55-year-old SSI(V) Johnny Boon, who had just extended his service for another three years, after having served VSC for 26 years.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As a full-time swimming and martial arts instructor, his skills were recognised and he was selected to serve as a training instructor.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Besides spending two evenings a week as a training instructor, he also took up additional policing duties, serving on Friday or Saturday nights at Tanglin Police Division.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: These officers, 734 of them, do not serve because of the $3.60 per hour.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If any Member of this House seriously thinks $3.60 is too much, then please let me know.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our VSC officers make considerable sacrifices to step forward to partner the Police Force.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They do not do this for the money.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, let us keep this whole issue in perspective.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the process, I have set out what happened.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Indeed, I have served and have had the distinction and honour to serve with many VSCs who served honourably through their many years in the Police Force.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have set out what we are doing.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We talked to AGC to look at the law.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: But the issue here is not payment: how much we should pay the volunteer corps.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Then, subsequently, the Minister decided to make it lawful by amending the regulations and approving retrospectively the seven years of overpayment.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: My question is: is this the correct way for the Government to make an unlawful payment lawful?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: And is this the way to respond to AGO's report on lapses?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: First of all, what is correct and not correct has got to go on the basis of the law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I think Mr Low heard me say quite clearly that what we have done is according to advice from AGC.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then, there can be an error in substance.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then there can be an error both in process and substance.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What happened here is a pure process error.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you look at that, and contrast with an error in substance, which may or may not have legal consequences, for example, let us say you have an association and there is going to be a challenge for the chairman at the annual general meeting.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Chairman quickly brings in new voting members to defeat the challenge.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But from the view of substance, is it correct?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Let us say a group takes over an organisation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It sets up a structure which helps to vacuum money out of the organisation and its own accountants say in writing, "Despite repeated requests, the organisation did not provide us with all the critical documents relating to the transactions with the friends"; and assume they repeat it every year and yet the organisation does not do anything.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is an error, both in process and in substance, and that is unlawful and that must have consequences.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Since Mr Low is so interested in this process error, I am sure he will be interested in errors of substance as well.
